assets.source_citation: IMO Polar Code (resolution MSC.385(94)), Part I-A, ship categories: A = at least medium first-year ice (PC1-PC5 or equivalent), B = at least thin first-year ice (PC6-PC7 or equivalent), C = open water or less severe ice conditions

values.category_C_ice_strengthening: none required or equivalent light ice class

assets.verification_note: Category definitions and the category-to-Polar-Class mapping are the widely reproduced content of Polar Code Part I-A; the IMO resolution text itself could not be retrieved in the build environment, so the mapping is high-confidence but not primary-verified.

assets.source_citation: IMO Polar Code Part I-A categories mapped onto WMO sea-ice thickness nomenclature: medium first-year ice 0.7-1.2 m, thin first-year ice 0.3-0.7 m, category C up to 0.3 m

tolerance.note: nomenclature band edges; 15% covers the WMO definition rounding

assets.verification_note: WMO ice-thickness class boundaries are quoted from the sea-ice nomenclature that the Polar Code category descriptions refer to; the WMO document was not opened during this build, so the numbers carry standard-reported, not verbatim, status.

assets.source_citation: IMO Polar Code Part I-A section 3 (polar service temperature, PST, derived from the lowest mean daily low temperature of the intended area and season): representative Arctic PST -30 degC within the -40..-20 degC band

tolerance.note: PST is area/season specific; -30 degC is a representative Arctic value

assets.verification_note: The PST definition (LMDLT of intended area and season) is the Polar Code content; the -30 degC value is a representative engineering value for Arctic seasonal operation, not a clause verbatim. Use the band for equipment/material ratings.
